messages:
Jess - CS: FYI ACME reported a sharp p99 increase for embeds starting ~2026-02-18 20:10 UTC, coincident with last night's infra rollout. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/ACME/embed-p99 :sob:
Maya R: ack. which infra rollout? CUDA/driver/firmware? any auth/billing noise?
Kevin (Infra): we pushed CUDA 15.1 + driver 525.60 and GPUFW 2.3.4 to eu-west1 at 19:45 UTC. No auth changes.
David (SRE): logs/traces? can you paste a request id or span? need to check KV-cache hit ratio and host io.
Jess - CS: ticket ACME-4892, sample request IDs: rQ_8a3f, rQ_8a4b. Attach: customer repro script and a short flamegraph they sent.
David (SRE): running quick check on one affected node, seeing io wait spikes and nvme queue-depth jumps around the same time as p99. looks like host-side IO stalls causing long tail on small embed batches.
Maya R: hmm. any change to cgroup or blkio settings in the rollout?
Kevin (Infra): no blkio changes. We did change driver build flags for NVMe power management in the packaging, and the firmware patch touched controller WCE handling.
ops-bot: deploy/infra: CUDA-15.1-driver-525.60 -> eu-west1 applied by infra-roller at 2026-02-18T19:45Z :white_check_mark:
David (SRE): quick mitigation options: 1) steer ACME traffic to a pool still on CUDA 15.0/driver 523.x, 2) enable KV-cache prefix caching for their route, 3) temporarily increase replica count for their route to hide p99. Which do we want?
Jess - CS: customer wants low-lift changes first. steer them if possible, we'll propose routing to older pool.
Kevin (Infra): we have a small set of eu-west1 nodes still on previous driver kept for rollback. can route ACME there. also starting a 2-node rollback canary now.
Maya R: David, can you confirm repro locally? Share small reproduction steps so we can validate whether it's NVMe contention vs driver-level scheduling.
David (SRE): repro steps I ran (very quick):
```
# simulate embed small-batch steady stream
python tools/repro_embed.py --endpoint /v1/embeddings --batch 1 --qps 20 --duration 10m --model rdx-small
# monitor iostat on node
iostat -x 1
```
On affected nodes iostat shows %util ~95 and avgqu-sz spikes to 40-80 under this load.
Maya R: ok that strongly suggests storage contention. can we tweak kernel block scheduler (noop -> mq-deadline) or adjust rq_affinity?
Kevin (Infra): we can flip elevator on a canary node, but it's risky for other tenants. prefer routing only for ACME while we triage.
FW-Team: looking at FW logs, the controller idle->active transitions increased after 2.3.4, will dig.
David (SRE): immediate plan: 1) route ACME to rollback pool (Kevin) 2) enable extra replicas / KV-cache (Maya) 3) collect fio qdepth profiles and nvme logs (David) 4) FW-Team to investigate controller telemetry.
Jess - CS: will inform customer and ask for hold while we move them.
Kevin (Infra): routing change applied for ACME at 20:05 UTC -> traffic now goes to driver-523 pool. monitoring...
ops-bot: routing-change: route ACME -> eu-west1-driver-523 applied by infra-roller at 2026-02-18T20:05Z :rocket:
David (SRE): preliminary numbers: p99 dropped from ~1.2s to ~350ms for ACME after routing. NVMe avgqu-sz also fell back.
Maya R: great. next: schedule full rollback window for 523 on subset and coordinate FW-Team with vendor on 2.3.4 telemetry.
FW-Team: vendor case opened VEND-2026-88, pushing logs and sample dumps.
Jess - CS: thanks all — I'll update ACME and close the customer-facing loop once we have rollback plan & vendor update. :thumbsup:
David (SRE): I'll keep collecting traces for post-mortem. please add any further notes here.
Maya R: adding incident tag INC-2026-45 and will start a short postmortem doc once we stabilize.
Jess - CS: closing thread for now, will reopen if p99 resurges.
